title: A Rivergate for the Current
premise: Felix Underhill, a desert ranger bound by a family debt to the mining consortium that owns her father's grave, is ordered to find a vanished government survey team in the Redglass Range before winter closes the passes and the concession permits expire. Tracking them, she discovers the team faked their disappearance to expose falsified mineral surveys that would displace the river settlements — and among them is Wren Calloway, the thief Felix has chased for two years, who stole not money but the original survey ledgers. Torn between duty to her employers and growing love for Wren and the river people, Felix must choose: deliver the evidence and lose everything she's owed, or bury it and become the thief herself. She crosses the range ahead of the snows, delivers the ledgers to the territorial court at Rivergate, forfeits her debt and her badge, and finds a new belonging on the water with Wren.
about_author: Silas Okafor is a former hydrologist who spent a decade mapping seasonal rivers across arid basins before turning to fiction. He writes adventure stories about landscapes that outlast the people who try to own them.

chapters.title: The Debt in the Dust
chapters.summary: Felix Underhill's POV. Establishes Felix tracking a petty thief through the flats outside Coriander Wells, failing again to catch the elusive Wren Calloway, and returning to face Consortium superintendent Harrow, who reminds her of the debt securing her father's grave plot. Emotional beat: weary obligation, the sense that her life isn't her own.

chapters.title: Gear Without Ghosts
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. A government survey team vanishes from a canyon camp — tents pitched, instruments running, meals half-eaten, no tracks leaving. Harrow orders Felix to find them before the snows close the high passes and void the concession permits. Emotional beat: unease sharpening into resolve; the first hint that nothing here adds up.

chapters.title: What the Compass Won't Say
chapters.summary: Felix's POV, intercut with Wren's journal fragments. Following an impossible trail up into the Redglass Range, Felix finds signs deliberately left — a boot print too clean, a cairn built wrong — as if someone wants to be followed slowly. Emotional beat: dawning suspicion that the disappearance is a performance.

chapters.title: Thief on the Scree
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Reveals Wren stole the original survey ledgers proving the consortium falsified mineral data to seize river settlement land, and joined the survey team's quiet defection. She spots Felix tracking them and must decide whether to lead her astray or let her come. Emotional beat: guilt, calculation, reluctant fascination with her pursuer.

chapters.title: The Camp Above the Clouds
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Felix corners the hidden camp at treeline; instead of arrest, she finds six exhausted surveyors and Wren waiting with the truth laid open — maps, ledgers, the forged reports. The team begs her to carry word down before the permits expire. Emotional beat: confrontation dissolving into crisis of loyalty.

chapters.title: Harrow's Ledger
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. A supply runner brings word: Harrow knows where they are and has hired cutters to retrieve the ledgers and silence the team; Felix's debt will be forgiven if she delivers Wren. Snow begins early. Emotional beat: betrayal crystallizing into defiance; love against duty made explicit.

chapters.title: Running the White Pass
chapters.summary: Ensemble POV. The descent begins — a race down the pass ahead of the storm and the cutters, crossing a frozen river, losing a teammate to a crevasse Felix barely saves. Wren and Felix trade watch shifts and truths by firelight. Emotional beat: trust forged under pressure; tenderness amid danger.

chapters.title: The Cutting at Stonebridge
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. The cutters ambush them at the old stone bridge; Wren is taken along with the ledgers, and Felix is left bleeding, offered one last chance to walk away clean. Instead she turns back toward Coriander Wells alone. Emotional beat: despair transmuted into choice — she picks her side.

chapters.title: Rivergate
chapters.summary: Climax, Felix's POV. At the territorial courthouse in Rivergate, with the permits expiring at dawn, Felix breaks Wren from the consortium lockup, recovers the ledgers, and stands before the magistrate as Harrow's men close in — testifying to the fraud at the cost of her name, her badge, and her father's grave. Emotional beat: sacrifice as self-definition.

chapters.title: A Current of Her Own
chapters.summary: Resolution, alternating POV. The permits are suspended pending inquiry; the river settlements hold. Debt-free but jobless, Felix takes a berth on Wren's survey barge, mapping honest water for the people who live by it. Emotional beat: quiet joy — belonging chosen rather than owed, and a future measured in currents, not debts.
